question: During the streamer's trip to Shanghai, when he left the Oriental Pearl Tower and continued his journey, how did he evaluate Chinese Oreos? 1. Quite good; 2. Suitable sweetness, not excessive; 3. Better than America's; 4. Not as good as Africa's?

rollouts.answer: 2. Suitable sweetness, not excessive — 'not too sweet', not compared to America/Africa.
rollouts.tool_call_sequence: read_skill x4 -> semantic_search/run_sql (implicit via memory-retrieval steps) -> clip_qa(170500-170620) -> submit

decisive_steps.what_happened: clip_qa sampled frames at 1fps over 170500-170620 then 4fps over 170550-170579 and concluded he only says the Oreo is 'not overly sweet / suitably sweet', explicitly denying the 'better than America' and 'worse than Africa' claims — it never surfaces 'quite good' or 'better than America's' as true, so the main agent submits option 2 only.

rollouts.failure_point: clip_qa under-extracted the spoken evaluation: it caught only the sweetness remark and missed the 'quite good' and 'better than America's' parts of the same utterance, then explicitly claimed those comparisons were absent.
rollouts.evidence_checked: DB episodes/topic_facts/semantic_triples around 170500-170600s only log 'spots a chinese oreo snack and decides to go get one' and 'ishowspeed says low-key days ... feel better than america' (a different, unrelated remark) — no structured row transcribes the actual taste verdict.

decisive_steps.what_happened: clip_qa sampled 0.5fps then 2fps over the eating interval and again reported only 'suitable sweetness / not excessive', denying the America/Africa comparisons, matching rollout-00's pattern.

rollouts.failure_point: Same as rollout-00: clip_qa consistently under-extracts to a single item (sweetness) and misses 'quite good' and 'better than America's'.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Same DB window checked; no structured evidence beyond the 'spots/decides to get' facts.

rollouts.answer: 1. Quite good — based on a later, unrelated remark at ~238,174-238,204s that he 'already tried Oreos in China and liked them'.

rollouts.answer: All four (1-4): quite good, not too sweet, better than American Oreos, not as good as African Oreos.
rollouts.tool_call_sequence: read_skill x4 -> semantic_search/run_sql -> clip_qa(170500-170610, 5 sample_video calls at varying fps) -> submit

decisive_steps.what_happened: clip_qa, after 5 rounds of frame sampling with no audio transcript available, returned a fabricated verbatim quote — 'They're good. They're not too sweet—better than American Oreos, but not as good as African Oreos' — that mirrors the four multiple-choice options almost exactly, including the option (4, 'not as good as Africa's') the question is designed to test as false; the main agent then submitted all four as true.

rollouts.failure_point: clip_qa hallucinated a complete quote that happens to affirm all 4 candidate options verbatim (including the trap option 4), rather than transcribing what was actually said; the accidental inclusion of options 1-3 (the true ones) alongside the false option 4 produced partial credit higher than the other rollouts' single-item answers.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Cross-checked DB around 170500-170600s: no structured row states 'better than American' or 'not as good as African'; the clip_qa quote is not traceable to any captured caption/triple, consistent with confabulation rather than grounded transcription.

db_evidence.notes: episodes/topic_facts/semantic_triples in the correct window (170508-170598s) only record the setup ('remarks about chinese oreos', 'spots a chinese oreo snack and decides to go get one'); no table transcribes the actual spoken taste verdict (the '1,2,3' evaluation). That verdict exists only in the raw video audio at source offset ~13306-14028s of video 14, so every rollout had to depend on clip_qa's own sampling/transcription of that segment, and clip_qa's outputs varied from under-extraction (only 'not too sweet', rollouts 0/1/3) to apparent fabrication of a full matching quote (rollout 4) to being skipped altogether (rollout 2 attempt-2).

root_causes: The structured memory tables (episodes, semantic_triples, topic_facts, visual_clips) never capture the actual spoken multi-part opinion about the Oreos — only the lead-up (spotting/deciding to buy) — so answering correctly requires accurate clip_qa transcription of that ~90s window, and no rollout got a clean, fully correct transcription from clip_qa.

clip_qa's sample_video tool returns frame images plus pre-existing (visual) captions, not a verbatim speech transcript, so the sub-agent has to infer spoken content largely from context; this produced inconsistent results across rollouts — three under-extracted to a single item, one over-extracted/hallucinated a quote matching all four multiple-choice options verbatim (including the deliberately false 'Africa' option).

In rollout 2, a malformed submit_answer JSON in attempt-1 discarded a completed clip_qa-grounded attempt; the forced retry (attempt-2) did not re-run clip_qa and instead answered from an unrelated, temporally distant DB snippet, yielding the weakest-grounded answer.

This is a hallucination-detection-style question (one of the four options, 'worse than Africa's', is a deliberate trap); no rollout correctly distinguished the trap option from the three true statements, so all rollouts scored partial credit at best.
what_worked: Four of five rollouts correctly located the right time window (170500-170628s, right after 'spots the oreo snack') via semantic_search/run_sql over episodes/topic_facts and invoked clip_qa there, avoiding wrong-window errors.
Rollout 4's clip_qa did recover 3 of the 3 true sub-claims (1, 2, 3), even though it also added the false 4th, giving it the best (though still partial) score.
transferable_lessons: For questions asking for an exact verbatim multi-part opinion/quote, treat the DB's episodes/topic_facts/semantic_triples layer as only locating the right time window, not as ground truth for spoken content — always dispatch clip_qa to that window and be explicit that it must ground its answer only in what is literally audible/legible, not paraphrase or extrapolate from the question's own multiple-choice wording.

When clip_qa's answer text repeats the candidate options almost verbatim (especially all of them, including implausible/contradictory ones), treat that as a red flag for confabulation rather than confirmation, and ask it to quote the exact phrase it heard/read plus timestamp evidence before accepting all options as true.

On hallucination-detection question types, explicitly instruct the retrieval/visual agents to actively look for evidence *against* each option (not just supporting evidence) since one option is a deliberate false lure; simply confirming 'this sounds plausible' is not enough.

If submit_answer fails JSON validation, the retry should preserve or re-run the visual evidence gathered in the failed attempt rather than falling back to SQL/semantic-search alone over unrelated distant matches.
open_questions: Whether the source video's audio actually contains all three of 'quite good', 'suitable sweetness', and 'better than America's' in one continuous utterance, or whether the reference answer '1,2,3' was assembled from a wider window than any rollout's clip_qa call covered — could not verify by listening to the audio track itself, only by inspecting frames and existing DB captions.

Why clip_qa in rollouts 0/1/3 consistently denies the 'better than America's' and 'quite good' claims (explicit negation, not just omission) — worth checking whether the sample_video tool exposes any audio signal at all, or whether the sub-agent is purely reasoning from silent frames and prior visual captions.
